source_caption:
Denzel Washington gives one of his most powerful performances in Flight (2012). ✈️

Directed by Robert Zemeckis, the film follows Whip Whitaker, a highly skilled airline pilot whose life is already falling apart because of alcohol and drug addiction. When a catastrophic mechanical failure sends his plane into a terrifying nosedive, Whip pulls off an almost impossible crash landing and saves most of the people on board.

But surviving the crash is only the beginning.

The investigation soon forces Whip to confront a question he’s spent years avoiding: was he really the hero everyone thinks he is?

The crash sequence is incredible, but what makes Flight hit so hard is what comes afterward. Denzel doesn’t play Whip as simply a good or bad person. He’s talented, deeply flawed, selfish, charismatic, and desperately trying to keep control of a life that’s slipping away.

The film’s plane crash was loosely inspired by Alaska Airlines Flight 261, including the terrifying idea of turning the aircraft upside down in an attempt to regain control. Unlike the movie, Flight 261 crashed with no survivors.

Zemeckis also used real MD-80 aircraft for the production, while Denzel and the crew had access to flight-simulator training to help make the aviation sequences feel authentic.

And Denzel earned an Oscar nomination for the role.

Have you seen Flight?

source_details.synopsis: Flight is a 2012 American drama film directed by Robert Zemeckis, written by John Gatins and produced by Walter F. Parkes, Laurie MacDonald, Steve Starkey, Zemeckis, and Jack Rapke. The film stars Denzel Washington as William "Whip" Whitaker Sr., an alcoholic airline pilot who miraculously crash-lands his plane after a mechanical failure, saving nearly everyone on board. Although hailed a hero, an investigation soon begins to cast the captain in a different light. Flight premiered at the New York Film Festival on October 14, 2012, and was theatrically released the following month on November 2, 2012 by Paramount Pictures. It received generally positive reviews from critics, who praised Washi
